exposure: Severe maternal morbidity (potentially life-threatening conditions, maternal near miss, maternal mortality)
Order of birth (first vs. second twin)
outcome: Apgar scores less than 7 at 5th minute
cohort: The study included 8,568 twin deliveries compared with 308,127 singleton deliveries from the WHO Multicountry Survey on Maternal and Newborn Health across 29 countries.
finding: Twin pregnancies are significantly associated with severe maternal morbidity and worse perinatal outcomes, with consistently poorer outcomes observed for the second twin.
cross-section timing: Data was collected during the WHO Multicountry Survey on Maternal and Newborn Health, assessing outcomes around the time of delivery.
